steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8-inch square baking dish.

Combine flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Mix egg, sour cream, milk, and butter in a small bowl. Fold egg mixture into flour mixture until just moistened; pour into prepared baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Corn Bread
raw_recipe.description: This cornbread recipe goes well with just about anything. I always make it when we have chili. The sour cream makes it nice and moist.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make sweet corn bread. A touch of sour cream helps it stay moist. Best of all, the bread's not overloaded with lard or butter, so it's nice and light.

review.reviewBody: Consistently good. I use a 9" cast iron round pan that I preheat in the oven, pull out and throw a couple of tablespoons of vegetable oil in before the batter. This gives it a lovely fried-like crust. I substitute yogurt for the sour cream and buttermilk for milk.

This is the best recipe I've found but it keeps coming out dry. I also doubled the amount of sugar to make it sweeter, but still dry. Can anyone help? Update- I now double the sugar, butter, and buttermilk. I also added 1/4 cup of extra cornmeal. Then also substituted in buttermilk and use half yogurt and half sour cream in the mix. I think it is important to soak the Cornmeal in the buttermilk for about 10 mins. It turned out to be out of this world. Moist, soft, and thick. 400*F for 30 min

I'm still making this corn bread recipe 5 years after my last review. 
I use Greek Low Fat Yogurt in place of the sour cream and it is fabulous every time!
After reading my last review of this recipe, I saw that I mentioned that I put the cornbread on top of a casserole; this is not our usual fare at home as we eat whole foods. But, when our oldest comes with her family it's fast and the little one loves it. She calls me Go-Go.
Go-Go's Hot Dog and Bean Casserole
In a sprayed oblong enamel pan, I pour in 3 cans of New England style brown baked beans. I cut up 2 packages of hot dogs (I use Hoffman's bc they are Kosher, so I know they are no fillers). I double the cornbread recipe and drop 6 dollops ( 2 x 3 ) around the pan and bake at 400 for 45 min to 1 hour, making sure the center of the cornbread is thoroughly cooked. Let it settle about 10 min before serving.

Delicious! Loved it Tweaked it a little. Added 2 eggs instead if 1. Used 1/3 cup sugar substituted buttermilk instead of milk. Melted a 4th cup butter in a 8 x 11 1/2“ baking dish. It was perfect. only took 15 minutes. Careful not to over bake

The only trouble we had with this recipe was waiting for it to cool! I did add a handful of frozen corn and a small chopped jalapeno for fun, and followed another suggestion of preheating the cast iron skillet and coating it with butter before the batter went in but followed the recipe for the rest. Will make this again to go with the next pot of chili! Thank you for anther great recipe!!

This recipe is delicious as written, but I added 1/4 cup of honey and doubled the recipe, putting it in a 9x13 pan instead. Took 30 mins to cook. I will always make this when I make chili. The bread is moist and the texture is smoother than any boxed corn bread. I also made honey butter with 1/4 cup honey and 3/4 cup softened butter. Delicious!

I went a little heavier on the corn meal and added a little extra 1/2 and 1/2 to compensate. I baked it for 30 minutes. It was probably one of the best corn breads I've ever made. Using sour cream really surprised me. It does not really stand out. I also used a pre heated black iron skillet with oil in it. Super delicious! This will be my "go to" corn bread recipe.

I don’t do many reviews, but this recipe is PERFECT!! I used 1 C Greek yogurt instead of sour cream and added 1/2 C sugar instead of 1/4 C. I also let the batter sit for 15 minutes to cut down on the grittyness. OMG! It is sooo moist!!

I really liked it, I pulsed some canned corn in the blender and put it in the mix for a little more moisture since I didn't have enough sour cream. I pulled it out of the oven just shy of 20 mins and it was perfectly moist!

This was the best sweet cornbread I have ever had. I did follow a recommendation below with extra sugar, butter and corn meal and used buttermilk instead of regular milk. Baked in a pre-heated iron skillet.

Per some notes by others, I increased corn meal to 1-1/2 cups and sugar to 1/2 C. I used half the sour cream and replaced the other half with plain Greek yogurt. I loved the result. This will now be my favorite corn bread recipe.
Very easy and tasty. I will be making this again. I made it exactly as called for and it turned out great

This turned out absolutely great. I added a little extra sugar because that's how I like corn bread. After I pulled it out and it was still hot I melted some homemade honey butter as well. Clearly I have a sweet tooth but it was a hit at my house.
Incredibly moist and delicious. If there is any leftovers try with cold milk poured over it for an added treat.

4 stars as-is. It's 5 stars with tweaks: an extra 1/4 c cornmeal, then used 1/2 c butter, 1/2 c sugar total. It was SO GOOD! bookmarked, this is THE recipe I'll use from now on! Also, it doesn't crumble hardly at all. It would hold up to dipping in chili, etc. Super moist and just perfect.
